messages:
maria (PM): uploaded a short PRD draft for the Console Observability launch guardrails — asking for quick sanity checks on acceptance criteria, cost/retention tradeoffs, and UX edge cases. link: https://drive.mock/redwood/prd-console-obs
kevin (Eng): skimmed it, looks good overall. main unknown is trace sampling defaults across Dedicated vs Hosted. do we force sample rate or make it config? :thinking:
maria (PM): prefer config but want safe defaults for Hosted (low cost). propose default sample_rate=0.1 for hosted, 1.0 for Dedicated by contract. open to pushback.
tara (Design): want to make the sampling setting discoverable in the route settings page. users should see an inline cost estimate before toggling. simple toggle + tooltip should work. mockup incoming.
omar (SRE): cost estimate needs to be backed by data — e.g., tokens/trace, spans per request. current telemetry is noisy. jess can we get a 30-day look for median spans/request by customer tier?
jess (Data): yes, I can pull a rolling 30-day for default models. will return numbers by EOD. also: retention windows impact storage cost nonlinearly — need discrete tiers (7d, 30d, 90d, 365d) and clear export/archival path.
maria (PM): adding that to acceptance criteria. key questions: a) migration policy for customers changing retention, b) UI/UX for selecting tier, c) billing backfill rules.
kevin (Eng): edge cases: customers with on-prem (Private) might have local retention rules — ensure console respects per-deployment policy. also, beware cascade deletes when we reduce retention -> need soft-delete window.
omar (SRE): +1 on soft-delete. propose a 48h quarantine before physical purge and an audit log entry for all deletions.
tara (Design): for the UX flow, propose a confirmation modal for retention changes that includes: estimated monthly delta, list of resources affected, and rollback instructions. keep modal concise.
jess (Data): for acceptance tests, suggest: 1) telemetry shows expected cost delta after tier switch in 7 days, 2) trace sampling toggles reflect in sampled-span ratio, 3) exports still succeed for archived traces.
kevin (Eng): technical acceptance criteria I'd add:
```
- default sampling implemented by deployment type and overridable per-route
- retention tiers enforceable via policy service with migration job
- soft-delete + audit log implemented
- fallback model route if trace export fails
```
maria (PM): great. can we all agree on launch M1: Hosted + Dedicated parity for those guardrails but Private will be opt-in (docs + config only)?
kevin (Eng): agree for M1. Private opt-in later, need infra changes.
omar (SRE): also add SLA considerations: for Hosted launches we should limit retention tier >30d to enterprise-only until we have cost alerts in place.
tara (Design): noted — will design enterprise-only badge and the confirmation copy for that state.
jess (Data): I'll add monitoring evals and a quick checklist for rollout: sample verification, retention purge test, cost-alert firing.
maria (PM): next steps: kevin to write implementation RFC for policy service and migration job (due Wed), tara to drop mocks (tomorrow), jess to provide telemetry numbers (EOD), omar to draft soft-delete/playbook (Thu). add reviewers: @kevin, @tara, @omar.
deploy-bot: PRD draft v1 uploaded to /prd/console-observability/2109876543, reviewers added: kevin, tara, omar :white_check_mark:
kevin (Eng): I'll start RFC and include the acceptance criteria snippet above. tagging infra and eng-runtime for apis.
maria (PM): thanks all — will consolidate feedback into PRD v1.1 after jess numbers and tara mocks. low-risk launch but lots of policy edgecases so calling this a "guardrails first" cut. :rocket:
